NKJV renders “you will not fear evil again” as “You shall see disaster no more,” reading the verb as “see.”
Close to the Hebrew; “let not your hands drop” is rendered “let not your hands be weak.”
NKJV renders “a warrior [who] will save” as “The Mighty One, will save,” and “he will be silent in his love” as “He will quiet you with His love.”
NKJV renders the difficult Hebrew as “those who sorrow over the appointed assembly … To whom its reproach is a burden”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “the outcast” is rendered “those who were driven out,” and “in all the earth their shame” “In every land where they were put to shame.”
